culture.title: The Crown Jewels at Rosenborg Castle
culture.description: A Renaissance pleasure palace in the King's Garden with a basement treasury holding the Danish crown jewels and a long hall guarded by three silver lions.
culture.bonus: Go down to the treasury last, not first.

culture.title: A Night at the Royal Danish Playhouse
culture.description: See theatre, opera or ballet in Skuespilhuset's waterfront box, then walk out onto the harbour promenade wrapped around the building.
culture.bonus: Have a drink on the deck over the water at the interval.

culture.title: Viking Ships and a Fjord Sail at Roskilde
culture.description: Five 11th-century ships excavated from the fjord, displayed in a brutalist hall beside the working boatyard that builds sailing replicas of them.
culture.bonus: Take the replica out on the fjord and pull an oar yourself.

culture.title: A Century of Chairs at Designmuseum Danmark
culture.description: The definitive collection of Danish modern design in an 18th-century former hospital — including a corridor lined with every chair that made the country famous.
culture.bonus: Pick the one chair you would actually live with.

culture.title: Hamlet's Castle at Kronborg
culture.description: The UNESCO-listed Renaissance fortress at Helsingør that Shakespeare called Elsinore, guarding the narrowest point of the sound with Sweden visible across the water.
culture.bonus: Go down into the casemates and find the sleeping statue of Holger the Dane.

culture.title: Underground Art in the Cisterns
culture.description: A drained Victorian reservoir under a Frederiksberg hill, still dripping and pitch dark, given over each year to a single vast site-specific installation.
culture.bonus: Stand still in the darkest chamber until your eyes adjust.

culture.title: The Winter Garden at Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek
culture.description: A brewer's private collection of Roman marble and French sculpture arranged around a domed palm court with a fountain — the most beautiful room in Copenhagen.
culture.bonus: Sit in the Winter Garden for ten minutes doing nothing at all.

culture.title: The Danish Golden Age at SMK
culture.description: Denmark's national gallery, where a glass-roofed sculpture street joins the old building to the new and Hammershøi's empty grey rooms are worth the trip alone.
culture.bonus: Find the Hammershøi room and stay in it longest.

8ball.title: Ride the Harbour Bus to the End of the Line
8ball.description: Board the next yellow harbour bus that docks, stay on it to the last stop, and start your day from wherever that turns out to be.
8ball.bonus: Do not look at the route map before you board.

8ball.title: Ask a Local What Tourists Always Miss
8ball.description: Ask the next Copenhagener you talk to for the one thing visitors never find, then go straight there without negotiating.
8ball.bonus: Ask three people and do whichever answer scares you most.

social.title: Tap Takeover at Mikkeller & Friends
social.description: Forty taps in a pastel Nørrebro basement from the brewery that made Copenhagen a beer city, with a bottle shop attached for whatever you cannot finish there.
social.bonus: Order the highest-ABV thing on the board. Just one.

social.title: See a Band at Loppen in Christiania
social.description: A 250-capacity room in a timber warehouse inside Christiania that has been putting on punk, noise and touring bands since 1973.
social.bonus: Go in without knowing who is playing.

social.title: Cocktails in the Townhouse at Ruby
social.description: An unmarked door in an 18th-century townhouse by the canal opens onto candlelit rooms and one of the best cocktail programmes in Scandinavia.
social.bonus: Find the door without asking anyone.

social.title: Late Jazz at La Fontaine
social.description: Copenhagen's oldest jazz bar, a small dark room off Strøget where the weekend jam sessions run past three in the morning and the musicians outnumber the seats.
social.bonus: Stay for a full set without checking your phone.

social.title: Pool and Pilsner at Bang & Jensen
social.description: A former pharmacy on Istedgade that runs as a café all day and turns into one of Vesterbro's friendliest bars the moment the light drops.
social.bonus: Win a game of pool against a local.

social.title: Board Games and Beer at Bastard Café
social.description: Several thousand board games, a bar, and staff whose actual job is to teach you the rules — a genuinely great way to spend a wet Copenhagen evening with strangers.
social.bonus: Ask a game guru to pick for you and play whatever they hand over.

social.title: All Night at Culture Box
social.description: Copenhagen's most serious techno room, three connected spaces near Nørreport that do not really begin until two and do not stop until the trains start again.
social.bonus: Stay until you can see daylight through the door.

social.title: Beers on Dronning Louises Bro
social.description: On the first warm evening of the year half of Nørrebro buys cans from a corner shop and sits on the bridge parapet over the lakes until it gets dark.
social.bonus: Talk to the group sitting next to you.

chill.title: A Slow Evening at Tivoli Gardens
chill.description: Walk the lantern-lit paths of the 1843 pleasure garden in the middle of the city, ignore the rides entirely, and stay for the open-air concert.
chill.bonus: Ride the wooden roller coaster from 1914 anyway.

chill.title: Sunset Swim at the Kastrup Sea Bath
chill.description: A spiralling wooden shell rising out of the Øresund at Kastrup, known as The Snail — a free, architecturally perfect place to sit, dive and watch the light go.
chill.bonus: Jump from the highest platform you are willing to.

chill.title: Records and Espresso at Sort Kaffe & Vinyl
chill.description: A tiny Vesterbro corner where the coffee is taken seriously and the racks of second-hand vinyl are the only other thing in the room.
chill.bonus: Buy a record by a Danish artist you have never heard of.

chill.title: Picnic Among the Poets at Assistens Kirkegård
chill.description: Nørrebro treats its historic cemetery as a park — people sunbathe and picnic on the lawns between Hans Christian Andersen and Søren Kierkegaard, and nobody finds it strange.
chill.bonus: Find Kierkegaard's grave without looking at a map.

chill.title: Watch the Elephants from Frederiksberg Gardens
chill.description: The romantic landscape garden behind Frederiksberg Palace happens to look directly into the zoo's Norman Foster elephant house — a free view of elephants from a public park bench.
chill.bonus: Find the spot where you can see them without paying.

chill.title: Coffee and a Long Read at Paludan Bogcafé
chill.description: A two-storey bookshop café near the old university where nobody will hurry you out of your chair, floor-to-ceiling shelves in every direction.
chill.bonus: Buy the book you end up reading.

adventure.title: Cross Every Bridge in the Inner Harbour
adventure.description: Walk Olafur Eliasson's Cirkelbroen, then Lille Langebro and Inderhavnsbroen in one route — three pieces of design you can actually walk across.
adventure.bonus: Photograph all three from water level.

adventure.title: Find the Wild Deer at Dyrehaven
adventure.description: Take the S-train to a UNESCO-listed royal hunting forest where two thousand fallow and red deer roam free among 400-year-old oaks, twenty minutes north of the city.
adventure.bonus: Get close enough to photograph a stag — then back off first.

adventure.title: Ski the Roof of a Power Plant at CopenHill
adventure.description: Ride the lift to the summit of Amager Bakke — a working waste-to-energy plant with a year-round dry ski slope, the world's tallest climbing wall and a hiking trail down its green roof.
adventure.bonus: Take the run without stopping once.

adventure.title: Walk the Colour Strips of Superkilen
adventure.description: Cut through Nørrebro's radical public park, built from objects sourced in the sixty nations its neighbours came from — a Moroccan fountain, Thai boxing ring and Japanese octopus slide in one strip.
adventure.bonus: Find an object from a country you have been to.

adventure.title: Cycle Out to Amager Strandpark
adventure.description: Ride twenty minutes from the centre to a two-kilometre artificial island of dunes, lagoon and open Øresund water where the whole city swims all summer.
adventure.bonus: Swim out to the far side of the lagoon and back.

adventure.title: Sauna and Cold Plunge at La Banchina
adventure.description: Sweat in a tiny wood-fired harbour sauna on Refshaleøen, then drop straight off the jetty into the Øresund — the most Danish thing you can do to yourself.
adventure.bonus: Stay in the water for a full sixty seconds.

adventure.title: Walk the Star Ramparts of Kastellet
adventure.description: Loop the grass ramparts of a perfectly preserved 17th-century star fortress that is still an active military site, ending at the windmill above the moat.
adventure.bonus: Complete the full pentagon without cutting a corner.

adventure.title: Cross the Øresund Bridge for Lunch in Sweden
adventure.description: Board a train at Central Station and be in another country in thirty-five minutes, crossing the bridge and tunnel that link Denmark to Malmö.
adventure.bonus: Eat lunch in Sweden and be back in Denmark by dinner.

foodie.title: Cardamom Bun at Juno the Bakery
foodie.description: Queue on an unremarkable Østerbro side street for what is widely argued to be the best cardamom bun in Scandinavia, pulled warm from the oven in batches.
foodie.bonus: Get there before the cardamom buns sell out. They do.

foodie.title: Sourdough and Pastry at Hart Bageri
foodie.description: Richard Hart left Tartine in San Francisco to bake in Frederiksberg, and the laminated pastry and dark sourdough here are the reason Copenhagen bakers now cross town for bread.
foodie.bonus: Buy a whole loaf and eat the heel on the walk home.

foodie.title: Natural Wine on the Canal at Ved Stranden 10
foodie.description: A wine bar in a set of old canal-front rooms where the staff pour by conversation rather than list, and you drink looking straight across at Christiansborg.
foodie.bonus: Describe what you want without naming a grape and drink whatever arrives.

foodie.title: Graze the Glass Halls of Torvehallerne
foodie.description: Work two glass market halls at Nørreport for smørrebrød, fresh fish, cheese and porridge, assembling lunch from six different counters instead of one.
foodie.bonus: Build a full meal without buying twice from the same stall.

foodie.title: Street Food Crawl at Reffen
foodie.description: Graze your way through dozens of shipping-container kitchens on the old shipyard waterfront, beer in hand, with the harbour on one side and a scrapyard-chic bar on the other.
foodie.bonus: Eat something from a cuisine you cannot place on a map.

foodie.title: Texas Barbecue and Beer at WarPigs
foodie.description: A Mikkeller and Three Floyds brewpub in the Meatpacking District serving brisket by weight on butcher paper, with twenty-odd taps brewed on site.
foodie.bonus: Order by the pound and finish what you ordered.

foodie.title: The Full Experience at Alchemist
foodie.description: Fifty 'impressions' across four hours in a converted naval theatre workshop, under a planetarium dome — the most theatrical meal in Northern Europe, and a genuine once-in-a-lifetime splurge.
foodie.bonus: Go in with no menu spoilers. Look nothing up first.

foodie.title: Oysters and Seafood at Kødbyens Fiskebar
foodie.description: Raw bar and Nordic seafood in a former meatpacking hall, all tile and steel, with a long counter built for eating shellfish over a cold glass of something dry.
foodie.bonus: Try an oyster from the coldest water on the list.
